title: Beau Lamarre-Condon trial live updates: accused double murderer gives evidence in high-profile case
summary: The 31-year-old former police officer is accused of fatally shooting couple Jesse Baird and Luke Davies in Sydney in 2024

blocks.text: Lamarre-Condon alleges homophobia under former supervisor
Lamarre-Condon has accused his former supervisor of making homophobic remarks while he was an openly gay police officer.
“He would say things such as, ‘I used to bash gay people while in Jindabyne,’” he told the court.
During one occasion when responding to a domestic violence report, the man allegedly said, “Let’s go get these fucking faggots.”
Former police officer Beau Lamarre-Condon has taken the witness box in his double murder trial.
He is giving evidence in the NSW supreme court in front of a 15-person jury, as the first witness for the defence.
Wearing a light grey suit, a dark coloured tie and a white collared shirt, Lamarre-Condon took an oath and vowed to tell the truth.
Welcome to Guardian Australia’s coverage of the Beau Lamarre-Condon trial.
Lamarre-Condon is giving evidence this morning in his high-profile double murder case in Sydney.
The 31-year-old is accused of fatally shooting couple Jesse Baird and Luke Davies with his police service weapon in Baird’s Paddington home on 19 February 2024.
He has pleaded not guilty to two counts of murder and one charge of aggravated break and enter.
